text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the exchange outputs, and the leaning (inconclusive) is cautious and consistent with the hybrid_review. But the summary is internally inconsistent in places, misdescribes some evidence, and its next steps are generic, so an investigator would have to redo some work.","problems":["Headline says \"all 30 random charts support the billed level\", but only 9 of the 30 are 99215 charts; the 99215 evidence is thin and the headline overstates it.","Rationale says \"Claims and charts disagree\" while elsewhere stating charts support billing; the contradiction is confusing and unexplained.","\"Many 99215s are for minor problems in young patients (URI, rash, back pain)\" is loosely grounded: rash does not appear in the card's dx codes, ages are mostly 27-69, and the cited claims are not young patients.","Cited examples are just the first two low-complexity claims (C0035231 hypertension; C0035237 R21), which are weak illustrations; no high-complexity contrast or chart-supported example is cited.","Next steps are generic. \"Re-screen once records arrive\" is vague, and the summary does not name specific claims for documentation request even though the closed request mentioned a targeted follow-on for low-complexity 99215s.","Says \"too thin to judge\" but the headline asserts all charts support billing; the sample was random, not targeted at low-complexity 99215s, and this limitation is not clearly flagged.","The by-complexity pattern (e.g., 20% 99215 at 0 conditions, 100% at 4) is only partly used."]}
